key_insight: A feed-forward pipeline fine-tunes a vision-language model to infer both garment geometry and material properties from a single image, producing simulation-ready garments without multi-view capture or costly differentiable simulation.
problem_solved: Recovering physically accurate, simulation-ready cloth (geometry + material parameters) from a single image — an ill-posed task made harder by the lack of image-to-physics training data and prior methods that require multi-view capture or only predict geometry.
method: Fine-tune a vision-language model to predict garment semantics and material attributes from a single RGB image.
Map predicted semantics/material cues into simulation-ready outputs (meshes/patterns plus material parameters) using learned priors and templates.
Use a fully feed-forward generator to produce ready-to-sim garments, avoiding multi-view capture and expensive differentiable physics during inference.
impact: Enables fast creation of realistic, physically plausible garments from a single photo—reducing data/capture needs and accelerating workflows for virtual try-on, game asset creation, and cloth-aware simulation in research and industry.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: single input photo → vision-language encoder → material + geometry prediction → simulation-ready mesh + params
Before/after comparison: original image vs. rendered simulated garment on a body
Material-parameter visualization: heatmaps or icons showing inferred stretch/stiffness/friction mapped onto the garment
Mesh & pattern overlay: UV/pattern view showing how predicted geometry maps to a cloth pattern ready for physics
paper_title: Image2Garment: Simulation-ready Garment Generation from a Single Image
paper_authors: Selim Emir Can, Jan Ackermann, Kiyohiro Nakayama, Ruofan Liu, Tong Wu
